source: NCBI PubMed EFetch via Sider Scholar

rows.title: Diet and Risk of Cardiovascular Disease.
rows.evidence_boundary: This narrative review integrates broad dietary evidence that is partly observational and confounded; it supports pattern-level interpretation rather than causal claims about any single food or supplement.

rows.title: Polyunsaturated fatty acids and psychotic disorders: integrating mechanistic, genetic, and clinical evidence.
rows.evidence_boundary: The review combines mechanistic, genetic, biomarker, and intervention evidence across heterogeneous psychiatric populations; it does not establish a uniform therapeutic effect of PUFA supplementation.

rows.title: Ginkgo biloba Leaf Extracts in Global Dementia and Mild Cognitive Impairment Guidelines. A Review.
rows.evidence_boundary: Guideline positions vary internationally and often concern standardized Ginkgo extracts such as EGb 761; recommendations should not be generalized to all Ginkgo products or prevention claims.

rows.title: Harnessing Medicinal Plants Through Advanced Drug Delivery: A New Era in Type 2 Diabetes Management.
rows.evidence_boundary: The review emphasizes phytochemical mechanisms and advanced delivery systems, much of which is preclinical or translational; clinical efficacy of specific formulations remains incompletely established.

rows.title: Creatine monohydrate supplementation for recovery from muscle disuse: Timing matters.
rows.evidence_boundary: Human disuse and rehabilitation studies are limited and timing-dependent; creatine does not consistently prevent atrophy during immobilization, so recovery-phase findings should not be overgeneralized.
